proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) satisfying the two hypotheses in the statement, and let
\[
\mathscr N_P=\sigma\{N_1(c_P),\ldots,N_{K_n}(c_P)\}.
\]
By \(\text{def:known-cutoff-threshold}\), \(\mathcal G_c=\{c_P\}\), so \(|\mathcal G_c|=1\).  Substitution into the threshold in \(\text{def:four-cell-calibration}\) gives, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_n(\delta_n)
&=3\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}\log\{N_k(c_P)+1\}
  +\log\frac{|\mathcal G_c||\mathcal G_\vartheta|}{\delta_n}\\
&=3\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}\log\{N_k(c_P)+1\}
  +\log\frac{|\mathcal G_\vartheta|}{\delta_n}\\
&=\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n).
\end{aligned}
\]
The hypotheses \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and that the certified outer program contains the true bin averages imply
\((c_P,\theta_P)\in\mathcal G_c\times\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and verify precisely the two premises of \(\text{prop:association-unrestricted-calibration}\).  That proposition and the displayed threshold identity therefore yield
\[
P\!\left\{\Delta_n(c_P,\theta_P)>\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n)\mid\mathscr N_P\right\}
\le \frac{\delta_n}{|\mathcal G_\vartheta|}
\le\delta_n,
\]
where the last inequality follows from the nonemptiness of the finite grid \(\mathcal G_\vartheta\).

By the definition of \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\) in \(\text{def:known-cutoff-grid-rule}\), on the complementary event
\[
\Delta_n(c_P,\theta_P)\le\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n)
\]
one has
\[
\theta_P\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}
\subseteq\operatorname{hull}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}).
\]
Consequently the conditional coverage probabilities of both the inverted grid set and its connected hull are at least \(1-\delta_n/|\mathcal G_\vartheta|\), hence at least \(1-\delta_n\).

Let \(F_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\) be the union of the certified fallback branches listed in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\).  Proposition \(\text{prop:wald-late-identification}\) gives
\[
\theta_P=E_P\!\left[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_P\right]\in\Theta;
\]
and the conditional causal contrast is well defined by the positivity premise already discharged in that proposition.  Hence \(\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}=\Theta\) on \(F_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\).  On \((F_n^{\mathrm{kc}})^c\), \(\text{def:known-cutoff-grid-rule}\) and the preceding acceptance implication show that the same conclusion holds whenever the true-label deviance does not exceed its threshold.  Pointwise,
\[
\{\theta_P\notin I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\}
\subseteq
\{\Delta_n(c_P,\theta_P)>\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n)\}.
\]
Conditioning on \(\mathscr N_P\) and using the calibrated bound gives
\[
P\{\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\mid\mathscr N_P\}
\ge1-\frac{\delta_n}{|\mathcal G_\vartheta|}
\ge1-\delta_n.
\]
Taking expectations with respect to \(\mathscr N_P\) proves the corresponding unconditional bound for \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\), its hull, and \(I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\); in particular,
\[
P\{\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\}\ge1-\delta_n.
\]
For completeness, each count vector has finite support, and \(\Delta_n(c_P,\vartheta)\), the certified fallback indicators, and the lexicographic tie rule in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\) are deterministic extended-real functions of that vector.  Therefore \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\) and \(I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\) are measurable; the latter is connected because it is either \(\Theta\) or a connected hull.

The uniformity assertion is inherited from \(\text{prop:association-unrestricted-calibration}\): its multinomial type bound permits zero joint cells and every binary association, and no residual-variance lower bound was invoked anywhere above.  Finally, the cutoff is supplied and \(\mathcal G_c\) is a singleton throughout, so neither the construction nor its guarantee uses a cutoff-recovery condition.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: If \(c_P\) is supplied to the rule, use \(\mathcal G_c=\{c_P\}\), the fixed-cutoff threshold and interval in \(\text{def:known-cutoff-threshold}\) and \(\text{def:known-cutoff-grid-rule}\), suppress cutoff profiling, and invert only \(\Delta_n(c_P,\vartheta)\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) such that \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and the certified outer margin program contains the true bin averages, \[P\!\left\{\Delta_n(c_P,\theta_P)>\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n)\mid N_1(c_P),\ldots,N_{K_n}(c_P)\right\}\le\frac{\delta_n}{|\mathcal G_\vartheta|}\le\delta_n.\] The inverted grid set \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\), its connected hull, and the fallback-safe rule \(I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\) each cover \(\theta_P\), conditionally and unconditionally, with probability at least \(1-\delta_n\); in particular, \[P\{\theta_P\in I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\}\ge1-\delta_n.\] These conclusions hold uniformly over every binary treatment--outcome association permitted by \(\mathcal P_n\), including zero joint cells and singular null residuals. By \(\text{prop:wald-late-identification}\), the covered parameter is \(\theta_P=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_P]\). No condition on the cutoff-recovery index \(\lambda_n\) is used. No full-continuum honesty, expected-length order, or first-order equivalence to residual-jump inversion is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original continuum-honesty, expected-length, and first-order-equivalence assertions require uniform local-polynomial and likelihood-comparison results absent from the established core. The existing four-cell calibration does prove the finite-grid fixed-cutoff specialization exactly when the cutoff grid is the singleton \(\{c_P\}\); the proposed claim states precisely that proved reduction without adding a model assumption.

proposed.name: \Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n)
proposed.construction: When \(c_P\) is supplied, set \(\mathcal G_c=\{c_P\}\) and define \[\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n)=3\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}\log\{N_k(c_P)+1\}+\log\frac{|\mathcal G_\vartheta|}{\delta_n}.\] This is \(\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\) from \(\text{def:four-cell-calibration}\) after substituting \(|\mathcal G_c|=1\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the exact singleton-cutoff specialization required by the directive and used by the proof.

proposed.name: Known-cutoff inverted grid set and interval
proposed.construction: For a finite nonempty effect grid \(\mathcal G_\vartheta\subseteq\Theta\), define \[\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}=\{\vartheta\in\mathcal G_\vartheta:\Delta_n(c_P,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{kc}}(\delta_n)\}.\] Let \(F_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\) be the union of the certified fallback branches listed in \(\text{def:worked-four-cell-grid}\), with cutoff profiling suppressed. Define the connected rule \[I_n^{\mathrm{kc}}=\begin{cases}\Theta,&F_n^{\mathrm{kc}}\text{ occurs},\\ \operatorname{hull}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{kc}}),&(F_n^{\mathrm{kc}})^c\text{ occurs},\end{cases}\] with \(\operatorname{hull}(\varnothing)=\varnothing\). Thus only \(\Delta_n(c_P,\vartheta)\) is inverted, and every listed certified fallback returns \(\Theta\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This gives the explicit data-to-interval map certified by the narrowed theorem and incorporates every already-enumerated safe fallback.

proposed.statement: If \(c_P\) is supplied to the rule, use \(\mathcal G_c=\{c_P\}\), the fixed-cutoff threshold and interval in \(\text{def:known-cutoff-threshold}\) and \(\text{def:known-cutoff-grid-rule}\), suppress cutoff profiling, and invert only \(\Delta_n(c_P,\vartheta)\). By \(\text{prop:wald-late-identification}\), the covered parameter is \(\theta_P=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=C,X=c_P]\). No condition on the cutoff-recovery index \(\lambda_n\) is used. proposed.justification: This is the fixed-cutoff calibration sanity check: a singleton cutoff grid removes location search while preserving finite-grid four-cell validity on singular association faces. It is not an expected-length or first-order-efficiency claim.
proposed.gap: Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) develop weak-identification-robust fuzzy-RD inference at a fixed cutoff, and Noack and Rothe (2024) establish known-cutoff bias-aware honesty. The present theorem proves only the exact finite-grid specialization of the association-robust four-cell calibration; continuum honesty, a length rate, and first-order equivalence are outside its proved scope.
proposed.consumer: Researchers with a reliably documented threshold obtain a certified finite-grid inversion with conditional and unconditional coverage under arbitrary admissible binary treatment--outcome association, subject to grid inclusion and outer-program containment; no precision guarantee is claimed.

prose_updates.tldr: For fuzzy regression discontinuity with a weak compliance jump and unknown cutoff, cutoff recovery and causal-effect informativeness are distinct. A legal moving-cutoff continuum yields the exact flat-face limit \(2(1-\alpha)\), while \(T_n\), \(\tau_n\), and \(\lambda_n\) give an explicit all-strength regime partition. The open kernel is the \(s=1\) critical decision value and a total support-wide interval based on a formally defined four-cell population profile. Finite-grid calibration covers every compatible treatment--outcome association, including singular cells. When \(c_P\) is supplied, the singleton cutoff grid gives conditional and unconditional coverage at least \(1-\delta_n\) provided \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and the certified outer program contains the true bin averages; no continuum-honesty, expected-length, or first-order-equivalence claim is made for this fixed-cutoff reduction. The conservative unknown-cutoff procedure's upper rate is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), where its named grid, sieve, stochastic, continuum-transfer, calibration, and fallback errors are negligible.
prose_updates.related_work: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the local Wald identification argument. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) are the direct weak-identification fuzzy-RD predecessor: their reduced-form inversion treats the assignment cutoff as fixed and known, so there is no cutoff/effect-label experiment or unknown-cutoff minimax connected-length problem. Noack and Rothe (2024, Theorem 1 and Assumption 1(iii)) provide known-cutoff bias-aware inversion under conditions supporting studentization. The proved known-cutoff benchmark here is deliberately narrower: setting \(\mathcal G_c=\{c_P\}\) specializes the binned four-cell method-of-types test and yields conditional and unconditional finite-grid coverage when \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and the certified outer program contains the true bin averages. It claims neither continuum honesty, an expected-length rate, nor first-order equivalence to residual-jump inversion. Porter and Yu (2015, Sections 3--5) and Tuvaandorj (2020, Sections 3--4) inform unknown-location analysis in predominantly sharp designs, without the weak causal ratio. Elliott and M\"uller (2014, Sections 2.1--2.3) show why moderate unknown breaks require a process experiment, but their parametric break problem has no H\"older recovery profile. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, equations (3)--(4) and Theorem 1) and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 4) inform nuisance calibration and weak-decision analysis. Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4) connect testing power to expected length over convex fixed-index classes; the cutoff-indexed class here is a translated nonconvex union. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022, Section 2) establish that fuzzy-RD validity restrictions reside in the joint outcome--treatment law, motivating retention of all four observed cells. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version, Sections 3 and 6) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty in a Bayesian model without uniform frequentist honesty or minimax length.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The main class has no outcome-variance, null-residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor. The known-cutoff theorem proves finite-grid calibration only: it requires \(\theta_P\in\mathcal G_\vartheta\) and containment of the true bin averages in the certified outer program, and it makes no continuum-honesty, expected-length, or first-order-equivalence claim. Its coverage is nevertheless uniform over all permitted binary treatment--outcome associations, including zero cells and singular residuals. The moving-cutoff continuum, its causal lift, the finite-sample Kullback--Leibler bound, the flat-face expected-length limit, the algebraic regime partition, the population profile separation, and finite-grid four-cell calibration are explicit claims to prove. The finite-positive decision values, full-model least favorability, continuum discretization, negligible fallback risk, and all-strength attainment are open-ended questions. The minimax lower comparison at scale \(r_n\) is posed on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\); the conservative finite-grid upper comparison is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No smoothness of joint cells, conditional independence, association separation, cross-side derivative matching, oracle cutoff, or known association nuisance is imposed.
